name: Secondary market

subjectOf.text: Exit by selling reputation tokens is more problematic for reputation than for other cryptocurrency tokens, because reputation is less fungible: a token's value is tied to the specific post in which the reputation was created and is subject to separate review.
subjectOf.abstract: This is more problematic for reputation than for most other cryptocurrency tokens, since reputation is less fungible because a token's value is tied to the post in which the reputation was created and subject to separate review. But in principle it could be algorithmically valued.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Reputation as Capital – How DAOs Upgrade Finance (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3949098
scope_conditions: a member wants to exit by selling reputation tokens at fair market value

subjectOf.text: Impact 1.0 impact markets fail on the demand side: they have more sellers than buyers, and many potential buyers would have funded those projects anyway, which removes the need for a secondary market and significantly reduces resale value.
subjectOf.abstract: Impact 1.0 markets typically have more sellers than buyers and many potential buyers would have done those 47 projects anyway thus removing the need for a secondary market. This imbalance of high supply and low demand significantly reduces the "resale" value
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Impact Investing Innovation - From Impact 1.0 to 3.0 (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4685567
scope_conditions: Impact 1.0 secondary markets for social impact credits

subjectOf.text: LER can be engineered outside the Howey test by keeping reward units consumptive as discounts or credits, non-yielding, unmarketed for appreciation, and by disabling secondary trading.
subjectOf.abstract: LER could be engineered to fall outside of the Howey test. This is possible by avoiding a reasonable expectation of profits derived from the efforts of others. LER voucher loyalty reward units remain consumptive as discounts/credits, non-yielding, and not marketed for appreciation.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Liquid Equity Rewards (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5454054

subjectOf.text: A favorable legal assessment of LER depends on four design features holding simultaneously: non-transferability, absence of a secondary market, absence of fiat redemption, and consumptive utility.
subjectOf.abstract: Most important for a favorable legal assessment is LER non-transferability, no secondary market, no fiat redemption, and consumptive utility.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Liquid Equity Rewards (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5454054
